root_cause_label: pip3 install placed fasttext in the MiniSWE virtual environment (/opt/miniswea/...) rather than the system-wide Python that the benchmark evaluates; the agent then patched and validated only that wrong environment, never touching /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fasttext/FastText.py
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent installed and patched fasttext exclusively inside the MiniSWE virtual environment while the benchmark evaluates the system-wide Python interpreter, so the fix was never applied where it was needed.
t_err_evidence: At step 2, `pip3 install fasttext` installs to /opt/miniswea/lib/python3.13/site-packages/ (visible in the installation output: 'Requirement already satisfied: setuptools>=0.7.0 in /opt/miniswea/...'), not the system-wide /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/ that the benchmark evaluates.
t_commit_evidence: At step 8, the agent applies the sed patch to /opt/miniswea/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fasttext/FastText.py. After this, the outcome is locked: only the wrong file is patched and all subsequent steps are validation in the wrong environment.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed that `pip3` would install fasttext into the system-wide Python interpreter, but it actually installed into the MiniSWE virtual environment at /opt/miniswea/. This unverified assumption propagated through every subsequent step, causing all patching and validation to target the wrong Python environment.
forewarning_evidence: At step 6, `python3 -c "import fasttext; print(fasttext.__file__)"` returned /opt/miniswea/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fasttext/__init__.py. This clearly shows fasttext was loaded from the MiniSWE venv, not from the system-wide /usr/local/lib/..., but the agent proceeded without noticing the discrepancy.
